about: Written by tools/gen-grade-ledger.js: every case of tools/fixtures/grade-golden.json whose verdict src/core/answer/check.ts changes, and the rule that changed it; reviewed is written by hand. src/core/grade.test.ts holds the grader to it.

rules.rule: Numbers are compared exactly in BigInt, the 1e-9 band and a tol included, not in floats.
½ ¼ ¾ ⅓ ⅔, the dashes ‐ ‒ ﹣ － and full-width digits are read.
A trailing period is dropped in a number, fraction or set box.
A number named with a letter (x = 3) is refused as named.
Text with no single reading (units, a symbol, words, an expression, two values) is refused with its reason.
A space inside a number is refused, not deleted.
A mixed number (1 1/2) is read by its value, 3/2.
Thousands commas (5,050) are read in a number or fraction box.
A number in parentheses ((7), (3)/(2)) is read.
A decimal equal to the key rounded or cut at its own places, with no tol, is form/rounded.
" or " and " and " separate the members of a set, as , and ; do.
±7 in a set is the two members 7 and -7.
A set member led by 0 and a digit (1,000 for the members 1 and 0) is refused.
A possible mixed number in a set (2 1/3, 2 and 1/3) is refused.
A set with exactly equal repeats whose distinct members pair with the key is form/repeated.
A point is compared by the exact values of its coordinates, in order.
A point in [...], <...> or with labels is form/notation.

reviewed.why: read by hand: the brackets hold the numerator and the denominator (N-bracket), so it is 3/2; the gate reads no bracketed number on purpose
read by hand: the division sign is a fraction bar (N-divide), so it is 3/2; the gate reads no ÷ on purpose
read by hand: the ½ character is the fraction 1/2 after the whole number 1 (N-unicode, then the mixed number), so it is 3/2; the gate reads no ½-style character on purpose
read by hand: the ½ character is 1/2, so 1 ½ is the mixed number 1 1/2, 3/2; the gate reads no ½-style character on purpose
read by hand: a thousands comma in a number box (N-comma), so it is 5050; the gate reads no thousands comma on purpose
read by hand: a leading $ (as the old grader took it) before 5,050 with its thousands comma (N-comma), so it is 5050; the gate reads no $ or thousands comma on purpose
read by hand: the brackets hold the integer 7 (N-bracket); the gate reads no bracketed number on purpose
read by hand: the full-width digit is 7 (N-unicode); the gate reads no full-width digit on purpose
read by hand: the brackets hold the signed integer -1 (N-bracket); the gate reads no bracketed number on purpose
read by hand: a minus sign before the bracketed 1 (N-bracket), so it is -1; the gate reads no bracketed number on purpose
read by hand: " and " separates the two members 2 and -7 (L-sep); the gate splits a set on , and ; only, on purpose
read by hand: " or " separates the two members 3 and -3 (L-sep); the gate splits a set on , and ; only, on purpose
read by hand: ± gives the two members 7 and -7 (L-pm); the gate reads no ± on purpose
read by hand: +- is ± and gives the two members 7 and -7 (L-pm); the gate reads no ± on purpose
read by hand: " and " separates the members 2 and -1/3 (L-sep), and the fraction is signed, so it is no spoken mixed number; the gate splits a set on , and ; only, on purpose
read by hand: " and " separates the members 1/2 and 1/3 (L-sep), and the first is a fraction, so it is no spoken mixed number; the gate splits a set on , and ; only, on purpose
